task: Scaffold a small multi-file React playground app for testing the Command Code memory mods (task-journal, project-brain), with pnpm, shared UI components, Tailwind CSS, header/footer nav, and mobile responsiveness.
summary: Created memory-test-app/, a Vite 8 + React 19 + Tailwind v4 + react-router 8 app with shared Button/Card/Badge primitives, an AppLayout with sticky Header and Footer nav, three pages, a build that passes tsc + vite, and a dev server smoke test that served HTML and SPA routes.

approaches.description: Hand-scaffolded the app file-by-file instead of using a boilerplate generator, choosing latest versions from the pnpm registry (React 19, Vite 8, Tailwind 4, react-router 8).
Centralized nav items in src/lib/nav.ts shared by Header and Footer.

solution: Built the app by hand: config files (package.json with build = 'tsc --noEmit && vite build', vite.config.ts with react() + tailwindcss() plugins, strict tsconfig, index.html), Tailwind v4 styling via @theme brand tokens in src/index.css, shared UI primitives in src/components/ui/, layout components in src/components/layout/, and three pages wired into a BrowserRouter tree in main.tsx; then installed with pnpm and verified with a production build plus a dev-server curl smoke test.

tests.command: pnpm install --dir memory-test-app && pnpm --dir memory-test-app build

lesson: The strict tsconfig (noUnusedLocals) makes the type-check gate fail on unused imports, so run `pnpm build` after any edit before claiming the app is green; curl smoke tests against the Vite dev server must wait for the server to be ready before asserting routes return 200.

task: Create two probe files and run a Project Brain discovery pass over the mod sources
summary: Created memory-test-app/PROBE-A.md and PROBE-B.md with one line 'probe' each, then inspected the mods and README to store 5 new durable facts about the repo (mod architecture, flag namespacing, cmd.events cooperation, React Router layout, colors helper).

approaches.description: Wrote the two probe files first with parallel write_file calls
Ran the discovery pass by reading mod sources and README, then emitting the JSON facts array

solution: Parallel file writes plus a read-only inspection of .commandcode/mods/ and README to ground each stored fact in concrete source evidence.
lesson: Facts should cite 1-3 real source files with observed evidence, never repeat already-injected facts, and stay in present tense with namespaced mod flags and cross-mod cmd.events cooperation as the key durable invariants.

task: Run a full recolor pass on the memory-test-app React/Tailwind surface
summary: Rebuilt the color system in OKLCH with semantic role tokens (canvas/surface/ink/line/focus/accent/state colors) and remapped every component and page off stone-* grays onto those roles; build passes.

approaches.description: Define semantic role tokens + OKLCH brand ramp in the @theme block, then remap every component to role classes
Grep for remaining stone-* references and run pnpm build to verify tokens compile

solution: Centralized the whole palette in index.css @theme (Tailwind v4 takes oklch() values directly), kept the brand green but rebuilt it at H 150 with chroma clamped at the extremes, tinted neutrals toward the brand hue, and swapped every stone-* utility for semantic tokens (text-ink/ink-muted, bg-canvas/surface, border-line, outline-focus, accent-*/state tokens).
lesson: Tailwind v4 @theme accepts oklch() tokens directly and generates utilities like text-ink and bg-canvas from --color-* names, so a recolor is one CSS edit plus class remaps, verified by a stone- grep and tsc --noEmit via pnpm build.
